newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Maastricht interim airport director to stand down.
newsitem.headline: Maastricht interim airport director to stand down.

text.p: Rob Lenterman, the interim director who heads Maastricht Aachen airport, is to leave his position at the start of 1997, the airport operating company said in a statement.

Lenterman will be replaced by Jaap Biemond, a former Schiphol Airport manager who has a reputation for the economic turn-around of airports. Industry sources said he is credited with successes at Rotterdam and most recently, Curacao airport in the Dutch Antilles.
Maastricht's operating company said Lenterman had been originally been named as interim director to oversee the airport's expansion plans.
However the statement said Lenterman felt he could no longer wait for Government clearance for a new runway and night flights.

A airport spokesman said Lenterman's interim appointment had been made as the airport's board of directors had thought their application for expansion would pass through Government in less than six months.

However the plan has been the source of ongoing discussions between the Transport and Environment ministries for the past two years, the spokesman said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
